en: Product cost per appointment per month

Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the days of stock to hold, the safety days, the wanted retail margin and attach rate, the count difference you accept and the days before a use-by date.

Check Items: the 35 back-bar and retail items with cost, price, reorder point, par level, supplier and lead days. Back-bar means the products used on clients, not sold. Update a cost or a price here first.

Read Stock Counts every week: the stock on the shelf, the days of cover, the items below the reorder point and the order quantity. Place orders and write them on Orders to Place; mark each one received on time or late.
Write every delivery on Purchases and every retail line on Retail Sales. The margin, the cost against the list cost and the monthly totals on Product Cost by Month fill in.
Count a few items each Friday and write them on Count History. The difference and its value show where stock goes: unlogged use, a missing purchase record, waste or loss.
Write waste and breakage on Waste and Breakage with the reason. Write batches with a use-by date on Batch and Expiry and use first the ones marked use first.
Fill in the Hygiene Log and the Steriliser Log every day. They are generic logs: check your own local rules for what you must record and keep. Redo any missed check the same day.
Keep Equipment Servicing up to date with the last and next service dates and Supplier Price Changes with every change in a cost. Check the retail price when a cost rises.
Use Usage per Service and Services to see the product cost of each service from the units it uses, and Laundry and Linen for the monthly linen cost.

Use the 14 calculators for reorder points, days of cover, product cost, back-bar forecast, stock value, retail margin, attach rate, count variance, waste, expiry, price rises, steriliser loads and equipment service.
Read the Stock and Hygiene Dashboard and the Charts every week: purchases, retail, waste, counts, hygiene and orders.
Close the till, see the profit per service and plan cash and growth
Close the till, see the profit and plan cash and growth
every trading day shows services, retail, prepaid sold, cash, card and transfer, with the counted cash and a till check for a drawer that is over or short
price less product and pay for each of the 20 services, per chair hour and after the studio overhead, so a service that loses money is flagged
studio revenue, retail and booth rent less product, pay and overhead for each technician and month, so you see who really earns for the studio
income, product, pay and rent and other costs add up by themselves to the profit, the margin and the profit for each appointment and each chair hour
fixed costs after booth rent against the margin kept on each appointment gives the break-even for every month and the safety margin above it
weekly cash in, cash out and the owner draw give the closing balance for 13 weeks and a warning when it comes close to or drops below your floor
cash now less the floor and the taxes you owe or hold shows how much the owner can draw without risking the rent and the pay run
a share of each month's profit is set aside, compared with what is needed, with the balance held before the next instalment
tax collected, due date, amount remitted and the tax still due for every month, with a check that warns before the due date
New chair and second room payback
setup cost, extra appointments and margin give the payback in months for a new chair, a new service or a second room, with a month by month scenario

One row per trading day: services, prepaid used, retail, prepaid sold, fees, cash, card, transfer, tips and counted cash; total takings, cash variance and the till check fill in by themselves.
Studio months with profit after product, pay and costs
One row per month: appointments, no-shows, minutes, revenue, studio revenue, tips, retail and new clients; costs, profit, margin and profit per appointment fill in from the other pages.
Service months with margin after product and pay
One row per service and month: appointments, revenue, studio revenue, product cost, technician pay and margin; the margin percent and the margin check fill in by themselves.
One row per technician and month: appointments, minutes, revenue, studio revenue, tips, retail and product; utilisation, pay, rent in and the profit contribution after overhead fill in.
One row per bill or cost: date, category, description, amount and who was paid; the share of the month fills in, so rent, insurance, software and card fees are easy to compare.
Pay runs by staff member and month
One row per staff member and month: takings, tips, hours, pay, booth rent, due date and status; the month end, days late and the pay check fill in by themselves.
One row per purchase from a supplier: date, item, category, kind, quantity, unit cost and amount; the share of the month and a check of quantity times unit cost fill in by themselves.
Amount less quantity times unit cost
Cash by month with the cost cover
One row per month: opening cash, cash in, booth rent in, staff pay, expenses, supplies, income tax, owner draw and closing cash; net cash, months of cost cover and the safe draw fill in.
Sales tax collected and remitted by month
One row per month: taxable sales, tax percent, tax collected, due date, amount remitted and status; the tax still due and the days to the due date fill in by themselves. Check your own local rules.
Income tax set aside from each month of profit
One row per month: set-aside percent, the amount set aside and any instalment paid; profit, the amount needed and the balance held fill in by themselves. Confirm the share with an adviser.
Takings by payment method and month
One row per month and payment method: the amount of completed visits and the number of visits; the share of the month fills in, so a shift to card, cash or prepaid sessions shows early.
Budget against actual by expense category
One row per month and category: the budget you set; the actual cost from Expenses, the gap, the gap percent and the budget check fill in by themselves.
One row per month: fixed costs after booth rent, the margin the studio keeps on an appointment and the appointments done; the break-even appointments and the safety margin fill in.
Packages, gift cards and memberships sold by month
One row per month: package sales, gift card sales and membership fees taken; the total and the share of the takings fill in, so cash that comes before the service is easy to see.
Booth rent income by renter and month
One row per renter and month: rent due, due date, amount paid, paid date and status; days late, arrears and the late check fill in by themselves. A booth renter keeps their own takings.
Growth projects with the payback in months
One row per idea such as a new chair, a new service or a second room: investment, extra revenue and extra cost a month, start and status; extra profit, payback and the return fill in.
One row per project and month of a ramp-up: extra appointments, extra revenue and extra cost; extra profit, cumulative profit after the investment and the check against the plan fill in.
One row per week for 13 weeks: cash expected in, cash expected out and the owner draw; net cash, the closing balance and the gap to the cash floor fill in from the cash you have now.
Services with margin per chair hour after overhead
The 20 services with minutes, price, product cost, deposit and standard pay; pay cost, margin, margin per chair hour and the profit after the chair-hour overhead fill in by themselves.

Team and outside contacts with revenue and rent
The owner, technicians, front desk and outside contacts with phone and pay model; studio revenue, profit contribution this month and booth rent owed fill in by themselves.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the overhead for each chair hour, the minimum margin, the sales tax percent, the income tax set-aside share, the cash floor and the owner draw.
Check Team and Services: the owner, technicians, front desk, outside contacts and 20 services. Margin per chair hour (what a service leaves after product and pay for each hour of a chair) fills in.
Close the till every day in Daily Takings: type the sales, the cash, card and transfer takings and the counted cash. Total takings, the cash variance and the till check fill in by themselves.

Add the bills to Expenses and the stock you buy to Purchases. Record pay in Pay Runs and the rent of each booth renter (a technician who rents a chair and keeps their own takings) in Booth Rent Income.
Read Studio Months at month end: income, product cost, pay, rent and other costs add up to the profit, the margin and the profit for each appointment and each chair hour.
Use Service Months, Technician Months and Services to see which service and which technician leave the most after product, pay and overhead.
Keep Cash Months and the 13-week Cash Forecast up to date. The forecast starts from the cash you have now and warns when a week comes close to or below the cash floor.
Use Sales Tax and Income Tax Set-aside to keep the tax money apart. Both pages are generic: check your own local rules and confirm the shares with an adviser.
Compare Budget with the actual cost of each category, watch Break-even and Payment Methods, and read Prepaid Sales for packages, gift cards and memberships.
Plan a new chair, a new service or a second room in Growth Projects and Growth Scenarios, then test the idea with the New Chair, New Service and Second Room calculators.
Use the 14 calculators for the till, profit, taxes and growth. Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send a text. Read the Profit Dashboard every week.
